title: Deliveroo take-home: cron expression parser
prompt:
Write a command-line application, in any language, that parses a cron string and expands each field to show the times at which it runs.
Handle the standard five time fields (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) plus a command; special strings such as @yearly are out of scope. The cron string arrives as one argument on one line.
Print a table with the field name in the first 14 columns and the times as a space-separated list after it.
Example input: "*/15 0 1,15 * 1-5 /usr/bin/find" gives minute 0 15 30 45; hour 0; day of month 1 15; month 1..12; day of week 1 2 3 4 5; command /usr/bin/find.
Spend no more than three hours; a correct subset beats something that does not run or is wrong. Treat the reviewer as a new team member taking over: include tests, a README and run instructions for a clean OS X/Linux machine.
follow_ups: Live round: accept day names such as MON-FRI in place of 1-7
Live round: add an optional year field
Live round: support further operators on some of the cron fields
Live round: extend the solution two or three times, adding a unit test for each extension and re-running the suite
